column1: # Slide queue: arguments worth showing, in the order they would be shown.
# Anyone adds a row when an argument is interesting; the author accepts or drops it.
# card: a card label, a chart (fig:<path>), or "-" for a question with no card yet.
# state: proposed (added, not yet accepted) | accepted | drafted (a slide exists) | shown | dropped
# The trace page shows each row with the card's proof state, so a slide never outruns its proof.

column3: the whole case in one contrast: the small benefit is checked end to end, the large risk checks itself
their best case fails on one inference, not on its aims
only we can save us written as policy: hold back in the lead, otherwise keep pace
harms documented and priced, benefits anecdote, at a like-for-like standard of proof
the people pricing AI ask about revenue, almost never about harm
every planet lens is a test; none can run until Anthropic meters its sites
what would the solution be if we really cared about the environment, the world and flourishing?

Wall Street will not discipline alignment: analysts ask about AI revenue about 5 times as often as about any AI risk or oversight, and 17 times as often as about control, regulation and harm (two-model proposal; the sales-goal inference is untested)
